accuracy_findings.claim: no building there can rise above its level
accuracy_findings.problem: Read literally, "no building there" includes the Megapolis itself, and the Megapolis does rise above its own level when upgraded. The brief says "no other building". The code cap exempts tile 1 (stellar_system.ex:391-395, `tile.id != 1`).

Every other sentence verified: infra on tile 2 or another building on tile 1 gives :wrong_building_type; queued infra gives :no_building_without_infra; destroy gives :infrastructure_are_not_removable; damage_tile skips infrastructure tiles (stellar_system.ex:1713-1714); habitable_planet is type :primary, so its tile 1 is the infrastructure tile.

votes.reason: Facts, card, level table and patent path are all instantly legible, but the one paragraph of prose packs a placement rule, a gating rule and an ongoing level-cap rule into one dense sentence with an ambiguous pronoun, so a player has to re-read it once.
stumbles: "no building there can rise above its level" — "its" could grammatically be read as belonging to "no building" itself (trivially true) rather than to the Megapolis, so it takes a second pass to land on the intended meaning (other tiles are capped at the Megapolis's current level)

"Until it is finished" reads like a one-time gate (build it once, tiles unlock), which sits awkwardly next to "can rise above its level" in the same sentence, which implies an ongoing cap that tracks the Megapolis's level as it's upgraded — not obvious on first read whether upgrading it later raises the cap further
"it only goes on that planet's tile 1" assumes the player already knows the tile-numbering convention; the link softens this but a first-week player may not have internalized what "tile 1" means yet

votes.reason: Facts, the tile-1/gating/indestructible rule, and the per-level cost-effect table are all clear on one read; only minor friction from a pronoun-heavy sentence and an inconsistency between the card and table.
stumbles: "no building there can rise above its level" — ambiguous pronoun referent (its = Megapolis's level, not the other tile's) takes a beat to resolve
Cost order flips between displays: card shows "120 Production / 8,400 Credit" but the level table columns go "Credit cost / Production cost"
Limited badge text "(planet, moon, asteroid)" sits beside "Built on: Habitable Planets," momentarily suggesting moons/asteroids are also valid sites

accuracy_findings.claim: Outside Flash games, the galaxy's first finished Metamaterials Factory is announced to every player in the Galactic News
accuracy_findings.problem: The qualifier is incomplete. Game.News.Server drops every event unless the instance is eligible. `eligible_speed?` rejects both :fast and :daily, and `tutorial?` rejects tutorial instances (news/server.ex:495-517). A daily challenge runs its own :daily speed on Legacy content (Daily.Generator @speed "daily"), and the Metamaterials Factory exists there. So a finish in a daily or the tutorial is never announced, although the sentence says it is.

rebuttals.finding: building/high_factory_dome and building/monument_dome must_fix #1, tutorial part: the fix wanted "Outside Flash games, daily challenges and the tutorial"
rebuttals.evidence: The tutorial is already a Flash game. Portal.GameController.tutorial_data/2 (lib/portal/controllers/game_controller.ex:85-355) builds the tutorial's game_data with "speed" => "fast" (line 354, no other def between 85 and 354). create_and_join_tutorial passes that instance to Instance.Manager.create_from_model/2 (line 56), and the manager stores String.to_existing_atom(game_data["speed"]) as metadata speed (manager.ex:368). So eligible_speed? already rejects it as :fast before tutorial? is ever needed. "Outside Flash games" was already true for the tutorial, and naming it separately would be redundant. The daily-challenge part of the finding is correct and was applied: dailies run at "daily" speed (lib/daily/generator.ex:43-45; key :daily in lib/data/game/content/speed.ex:26), which news/server.ex:512 rejects.

accuracy_findings.claim: Outside Flash games and daily challenges, the Galactic News announces the galaxy's first finished {name:building.high_factory_dome} to every player, with its faction and system.
accuracy_findings.problem: Edge case. The news event is only sent when the system has an owner (stellar_system.ex:1189-1190, `state.owner != nil`). Abandon sets `owner: nil` (stellar_system.ex:277), and by human decision the queue keeps running after an Abandon. So if the galaxy's first one finishes in a system after it was abandoned, nothing is announced and the 'first' is not used up. The next one finished in an owned system is then announced as the first. The two previous must_fix are resolved. The tutorial runs at "speed" => "fast" (game_controller.ex:354), which becomes metadata :speed (manager.ex:368), so `eligible_speed?` already rejects it and 'Outside Flash games and daily challenges' covers every ineligible instance. 'See [[game-time]]' compiles to /help/game-time, and that page names Flash in its speed table and mentions dailies.
accuracy_findings.fix: Optional: 'the galaxy's first {name:building.high_factory_dome} finished in a player's system'. Or leave it as it is, since the case is rare.
accuracy_findings.evidence: news/server.ex:95-104 and 495-517 (only :fast/:daily speeds and tutorial instances are ineligible); game_controller.ex:354 (tutorial speed fast); manager.ex:368 (`speed: String.to_existing_atom(game_data["speed"])`); compiled HTML: '... with its faction and system. See Game time.'; lint 0 errors (the 3 warnings also appear with --only building/infra_open, so they come from other pages).
